# Sirach Chapter 29 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 29 | **Date:** 2026-03-17

---

**29:1** The merciful person lends to their neighbor; the one who extends a helping hand is keeping the commandments.

**29:2** Lend to your neighbor when he needs it; and pay your neighbor back when it's his turn.

**29:3** Keep your word and deal honestly, and you'll find what you need when you need it.

**29:4** Many people have treated a loan like found money, and caused nothing but grief to the people who helped them.

**29:5** Before he gets the money he's kissing his neighbor's hands, speaking in humble tones about borrowing; but when payback time comes, he drags his feet, complains, and blames the circumstances.

**29:6** If he can scrape anything together, he pays back barely half and acts like he's done you a favor; if he can't, he just takes your money and turns you into an enemy for nothing. He pays you back with insults where you deserved thanks.

**29:7** Many people have refused to lend — not out of meanness, but because they've been taken advantage of before and can't afford it again.

**29:8** Even so, be patient with someone who's struggling, and don't make them wait for your help.

**29:9** Help the poor because the commandment says so; give according to what they need and don't turn them away empty-handed.

**29:10** Spend your money on a brother and a friend; don't let it rust away buried under a stone.

**29:11** Invest your treasure in keeping the commandments of the Most High, and it will pay you back better than gold.

**29:12** Store up generosity in your account and it will bail you out of every trouble.

**29:13** It fights on your behalf against your enemies better than the best shield or the heaviest spear.

**29:14** A good person puts up security for their neighbor; a shameless person abandons them.

**29:15** Don't forget what your guarantor did for you — they put their life on the line.

**29:16** A sinful person will destroy their guarantor's assets,

**29:17** and an ungrateful person will walk away from the one who saved them.

**29:18** Guaranteeing loans has wrecked many prosperous households — rocked them like a storm wave. It's driven capable people to wander as refugees in foreign countries.

**29:19** A sinner who keeps cosigning and making deals will end up in court.

**29:20** Help your neighbor as much as you can — but be careful, don't go down with them.

**29:21** The basics of life: water, bread, clothing, and a roof over your head.

**29:22** A poor man's life under a rough shelter is better than fancy food at someone else's table as a dependent.

**29:23** Be content with little or much — then you won't have to hear the snubs that come with living off others.

**29:24** Moving from house to house is a miserable way to live; wherever you're a guest, you can't even speak your mind freely.

**29:25** You host people and pour them drinks and get no thanks; on top of that you hear sharp words:

**29:26** "Come on, stranger, lay the table — if you've got anything, put it out."

**29:27** "Clear off, stranger — make way for someone important. My brother's here and I need the room."

**29:28** A generous person finds it hard to take: all the reproach about visits and loans and money.
